Assume Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine $d$-simplex and let
$G\in C^1(\overline K;\mathbb R^d)$. If $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit
normal on each facet $F$, then
$$\int_K\operatorname{div}G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_FG\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS.$$
For an orientation-preserving affine map $F_K(\widehat x)=b+A\widehat x$,
the oriented area element transforms as
$$n_{K,F}\,dS=\det(A)A^{-T}\widehat n_{\widehat F}\,d\widehat S.$$

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \ge 1$ and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$.

1. **Fundamental theorem, second part, in $\mathbb{R}^{m}$.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be differentiable at every point of $[a,b]$ as
   a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), and
   suppose $f' : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ is integrable. Then
   $$\int_a^b f' \;=\; f(b) - f(a).$$
2. **A bounded derivative gives a Lipschitz function.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable at
   every point of $(a,b)$, and let $M \ge 0$ satisfy
   $\lVert f'(t)\rVert_2 \le M$ for every $t \in (a,b)$. Then
   $$\lVert f(t) - f(s)\rVert_2 \;\le\; M\,|t-s| \qquad \text{for all } s,t \in [a,b],$$
   that is, $f$ is Lipschitz with constant $M$ as a map
   $([a,b], d_{\mathbb{R}}) \to (\mathbb{R}^{m}, d_2)$
   ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]], [[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]],
   [[lem-metrics-on-rn]]).

Orient every top-dimensional cell of a matching simplicial mesh by the
ambient orientation of $\mathbb R^d$, and orient each facet by the induced
boundary convention of [[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]]. In the sum
of the oriented boundaries of all top-dimensional cells, every interior
facet occurs twice with opposite signs; every boundary facet occurs once.

Let $a<b$ and choose an integer $N\ge1$ and points
$$a=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_N=b.$$
The **oriented interval mesh** is the ordered family of cells $I_j=(x_{j-1},x_j)$, $1\le j\le N$, each oriented from left to right. Write $h_j=x_j-x_{j-1}>0$. For an integer $p\ge0$, the **broken polynomial space** is
$$V_h^{\mathrm{br}}=\prod_{j=1}^N\mathbb P_p(I_j),$$
with functions interpreted cell by cell. At an interior node $x_j$, write $w^-_j=w|_{I_j}(x_j)$ for the trace from the left cell and $w^+_j=w|_{I_{j+1}}(x_j)$ for the trace from the right cell; the chosen face normal points from left to right, and the jump is $[w]_j=w^+_j-w^-_j$. At $a$ and $b$, the outward normals are $-1$ and $+1$, respectively.

The published matching-affine-simplicial-mesh convention used elsewhere on the A page has dimension $d\ge2$. This definition supplies the distinct one-dimensional interval and trace convention; it makes no assertion about multidimensional cells.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

When $d\ge2$, since $\beta$ is constant, $-\int_K\beta u_h\cdot\nabla u_h=-\frac12\int_K\operatorname{div}(\beta u_h^2)=-\frac12\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(\beta\cdot n_{K,F})u_h^2$ by [F2] and [A1]. When $d=1$ and $K=(x_{j-1},x_j)$, [F3] gives the same endpoint identity $-\int_K\beta u_h\,\partial_xu_h=-\frac12\sum_{e\in\partial K}(\beta n_{K,e})u_h(e)^2$. Sum over cells; [F4] pairs opposite normals on each interior facet for $d\ge2$, and [F5] gives opposite normals at every shared interval endpoint.

Fix an interior facet oriented from $K^-$ to $K^+$ and put $b=\beta\cdot n_F$. The two face terms from step 1.1 and the two upwind numerical-flux terms combine to $-\frac b2((u^-)^2-(u^+)^2)+b\widehat u(u^--u^+)$. If $b>0$, then $\widehat u=u^-$ and this is $\frac b2(u^+-u^-)^2$; if $b<0$, then $\widehat u=u^+$ and this is $\frac{|b|}{2}(u^+-u^-)^2$. For $b=0$ it vanishes. This scalar calculation also applies to the single endpoint quadrature in dimension one.

On an outflow boundary face, $b=\beta\cdot n>0$ and $\widehat u=u_h$, so the volume and flux terms combine to $\frac b2u_h^2$. On an inflow face, $b<0$ and $\widehat u=g$, so they combine to $\frac{|b|}{2}u_h^2-|b|gu_h=\frac{|b|}{2}(u_h-g)^2-\frac{|b|}{2}g^2$. Faces with $b=0$ contribute zero.

Substituting the interior contribution from step 2.1 and the boundary contributions from step 2.2 into the sum of the tested DG equations gives the displayed identity. All terms on the left after the time derivative are nonnegative; setting $g=0$ proves the final stability statement.

Let $K$ be a cell in the one-dimensional interval or $d\ge2$ matching affine-simplex branch of [[def-pe04-upwind-dg-transport-discretization]], and fix an integer degree $p\ge0$. Let $(K,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a finite measure space as in [[def-measure-space]], let $\mathcal L^2(\mu)$ have the raw measurable-function meaning of [[def-calligraphic-l-p-on-a-measure-space]], and let $W=\mathbb P_p(K)\subseteq\mathcal L^2(\mu)$. For $u\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$ define its **cellwise L2 projection relation** to be the set
$$\mathcal P_K(u)=\left\{p\in\mathbb P_p(K):\int_K(u-p)w\,d\mu=0\text{ for every }w\in\mathbb P_p(K)\right\}.$$
For a mesh, the broken relation is the product of these cell relations. The measure $\mu$ is required to give positive measure to every nonempty relatively open subset of $K$ when existence and uniqueness are claimed. This definition does not itself assert that the set is a singleton. Whenever a later result proves that the relation has a unique member, write $\Pi_Ku$ for that member.

If $f,g\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$, then

$$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_2\|g\|_2.$$

Equality holds if and only if at least one of $f,g$ is zero almost everywhere,
or there is a constant $c>0$ with

$$|f|^2=c\,|g|^2\qquad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.$$

derivations.claim: Choose the finite monomial basis $\{\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_M\}$ of $\mathbb P_p(K)$. Its Gram matrix $G_{ij}=\int_K\phi_i\phi_j\,d\mu$ is positive definite: for every nonzero coefficient vector $c$, the polynomial $q=\sum_i c_i\phi_i$ is continuous and nonzero at some point of $K$, so it is bounded away from zero on a nonempty relatively open subset; full support gives $c^TGc=\int_Kq^2\,d\mu>0$. Each moment $b_i=\int_Ku\phi_i\,d\mu$ is finite by [F2]. The invertible system $Gc=b$ therefore has a unique solution, and $p=\sum_i c_i\phi_i$ satisfies [F1].

For any $w\in\mathbb P_p(K)$, write $u-w=(u-\Pi_Ku)+(\Pi_Ku-w)$. The first term is orthogonal to the second by [F1], hence $\|u-w\|_2^2=\|u-\Pi_Ku\|_2^2+\|\Pi_Ku-w\|_2^2\ge\|u-\Pi_Ku\|_2^2$. Taking square roots proves best approximation.

On an affine element in dimension $d\ge1$, diagonal-norm SBP data consist of a nodal state vector with $N_K$ entries, a positive diagonal matrix $H_K\in\mathbb R^{N_K\times N_K}$, and derivative matrices $D_{K,\ell}$, $1\le\ell\le d$. Put $Q_{K,\ell}=H_KD_{K,\ell}$. For each face $F$ let $R_{K,F}$ select its face nodes from the volume nodes, let $M_{K,F}$ be a positive diagonal face quadrature matrix, and let $n_{K,F}$ be its constant outward unit normal. The data are **SBP compatible** when
$$D_{K,\ell}\mathbf1=0,\qquad R_{K,F}\mathbf1=\mathbf1_F,\qquad Q_{K,\ell}+Q_{K,\ell}^{T}=\sum_{F\subset\partial K} n_{K,F,\ell}R_{K,F}^{T}M_{K,F}R_{K,F}$$
for each coordinate $\ell$. The rows of $R_{K,F}$ select the nodes used by the face quadrature; on an interior face, the two cells have the same face nodes and weights under the face identification and opposite normals. In dimension one, $R_L$ and $R_R$ select the left and right endpoint nodes with normals $-1$ and $+1$.

This is conditional algebraic data: the definition does not assert that every mesh has such a rule. The identities include exact affine metric factors and no curved-element metric approximation.

Fix constant transport velocity $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ and SBP data from [[def-pe04-diagonal-norm-sbp-element-data]]. For each cell $K$, let $U_K(t)$ be the vector of nodal values, $Q_{K,\ell}=H_KD_{K,\ell}$, and $U_{K,F}=R_{K,F}U_K$. Set $b_{K,F}=\beta\cdot n_{K,F}$. At each interior face, use the trace from the cell with positive outward speed when $b_{K,F}>0$, and the neighboring trace when $b_{K,F}<0$; at boundary faces use the inflow data on $b_{K,F}<0$ and the interior trace on $b_{K,F}\ge0$. Denote this upwind scalar trace by $\widehat U_{K,F}$.

The **upwind SBP-SAT semidiscretization** is
$$H_K\dot U_K+\sum_{\ell=1}^d\beta_\ell Q_{K,\ell}U_K+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}R_{K,F}^{T}M_{K,F}\,b_{K,F}(\widehat U_{K,F}-U_{K,F})=0.$$
The sign of the SAT correction is fixed by this equation. The definition is spatial only and makes no fully discrete claim.

Including the SAT term, the cell energy equation is
$$\frac12\frac{d}{dt}(U_K^TH_KU_K)+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\left(b_{K,F}\widehat U_{K,F}^TM_{K,F}U_{K,F}-\frac{b_{K,F}}2U_{K,F}^TM_{K,F}U_{K,F}\right)=0.$$

If $b_F>0$, both upwind traces are $U^-_{F,q}$, so the two contributions in step 1.1 sum to $\frac{\omega_{F,q}b_F}{2}(U^-_{F,q}-U^+_{F,q})^2$. Let $(K,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a finite measure space as in [[def-measure-space]], let $\mathcal L^2(\mu)$ have the raw measurable-function meaning of [[def-calligraphic-l-p-on-a-measure-space]], and let $W=\mathbb P_p(K)\subseteq\mathcal L^2(\mu)$. For $u\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$ define its **cellwise L2 projection relation** to be the set
$$\mathcal P_K(u)=\left\{p\in\mathbb P_p(K):\int_K(u-p)w\,d\mu=0\text{ for every }w\in\mathbb P_p(K)\right\}.$$
For a mesh, the broken relation is the product of these cell relations. The measure $\mu$ is required to give positive measure to every nonempty relatively open subset of $K$ when existence and uniqueness are claimed. This definition does not itself assert that the set is a singleton. Whenever a later result proves that the relation has a unique member, write $\Pi_Ku$ for that member.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine $d$-simplex and let
$G\in C^1(\overline K;\mathbb R^d)$. If $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit
normal on each facet $F$, then
$$\int_K\operatorname{div}G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_FG\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS.$$
For an orientation-preserving affine map $F_K(\widehat x)=b+A\widehat x$,
the oriented area element transforms as
$$n_{K,F}\,dS=\det(A)A^{-T}\widehat n_{\widehat F}\,d\widehat S.$$

Orient every top-dimensional cell of a matching simplicial mesh by the
ambient orientation of $\mathbb R^d$, and orient each facet by the induced
boundary convention of [[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]]. In the sum
of the oriented boundaries of all top-dimensional cells, every interior
facet occurs twice with opposite signs; every boundary facet occurs once.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $n\ge1$, let $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $r>0$. Then the Euclidean ball $B(x,r)$ is
Lebesgue measurable and satisfies
$$0<\lambda(B(x,r))<\infty.$$

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

Let $a<b$ and choose an integer $N\ge1$ and points
$$a=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_N=b.$$
The **oriented interval mesh** is the ordered family of cells $I_j=(x_{j-1},x_j)$, $1\le j\le N$, each oriented from left to right. Write $h_j=x_j-x_{j-1}>0$. For an integer $p\ge0$, the **broken polynomial space** is
$$V_h^{\mathrm{br}}=\prod_{j=1}^N\mathbb P_p(I_j),$$
with functions interpreted cell by cell. At an interior node $x_j$, write $w^-_j=w|_{I_j}(x_j)$ for the trace from the left cell and $w^+_j=w|_{I_{j+1}}(x_j)$ for the trace from the right cell; the chosen face normal points from left to right, and the jump is $[w]_j=w^+_j-w^-_j$. At $a$ and $b$, the outward normals are $-1$ and $+1$, respectively.

The published matching-affine-simplicial-mesh convention used elsewhere on the A page has dimension $d\ge2$. This definition supplies the distinct one-dimensional interval and trace convention; it makes no assertion about multidimensional cells.

Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then

$$\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^n) \;\subseteq\; \mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n) :$$

every Borel subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) is Lebesgue
measurable ([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]). In
particular every open set, every closed set and every countable intersection of
open sets is Lebesgue measurable.

Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then:

1. $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a sigma-algebra on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and
   $\lambda_n$ is a measure on it ([[def-measure]]);
2. the measure space $(\mathbb{R}^n, \mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n), \lambda_n)$ is
   complete ([[def-complete-measure-space]]), and every $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$
   with $\lambda_n^*(S) = 0$ is Lebesgue measurable with $\lambda_n(S) = 0$;
3. every elementary set is Lebesgue measurable and
   $\lambda_n(A) = \mu_0(A)$ for every $A \in \mathcal{E}_n$; in particular
   $\lambda_n(B) = \operatorname{vol}(B)$ for every half-open box $B$,
   $\lambda_n(\varnothing) = 0$ and $\lambda_n(\mathbb{R}^n) = +\infty$.
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $(X,\mathcal A)$. If $A,B\in\mathcal A$ and $A\subseteq B$, then $\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$.

For every finite measure $\mu$ on a bounded nondegenerate interval or nondegenerate affine simplex $K$ that assigns positive measure to every nonempty relatively open subset, every $p\ge0$, and every $u\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$, the set $\mathcal P_K(u)$ in [[def-pe04-cellwise-l2-projection]] contains exactly one polynomial $\Pi_Ku$. For each $w\in\mathbb P_p(K)$,
$$\|u-\Pi_Ku\|_{L^2(K)}\le\|u-w\|_{L^2(K)}.$$

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \ge 1$ and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$.

1. **Fundamental theorem, second part, in $\mathbb{R}^{m}$.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be differentiable at every point of $[a,b]$ as
   a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), and
   suppose $f' : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ is integrable. Then
   $$\int_a^b f' \;=\; f(b) - f(a).$$
2. **A bounded derivative gives a Lipschitz function.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable at
   every point of $(a,b)$, and let $M \ge 0$ satisfy
   $\lVert f'(t)\rVert_2 \le M$ for every $t \in (a,b)$. Then
   $$\lVert f(t) - f(s)\rVert_2 \;\le\; M\,|t-s| \qquad \text{for all } s,t \in [a,b],$$

   ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]], [[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]],
   [[lem-metrics-on-rn]]).

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Multiplying the exact PDE by $w\in\mathbb P_p(K)$ and integrating by parts with [F3] when $d\ge2$ gives its weak equation. When $d=1$, apply [F12] to the product $\beta u w$ on each interval to obtain the same endpoint weak equation. In both branches the exact inflow trace is $g$ and the outflow trace is the exact upwind trace.

For $d\ge2$, each cell is a nondegenerate simplex whose interior is dense in the cell by [F6]. Every nonempty relatively open subset therefore intersects the interior in a nonempty Euclidean-open set, which contains a Euclidean ball. For $d=1$, each cell is an open interval by [F7], so every nonempty relatively open subset contains a Euclidean ball. In either branch [F5] and [A1] give that ball positive Lebesgue measure. Thus Lebesgue measure has full support on every cell.

Each cell is bounded and Borel: this follows from the interval description [F7] when $d=1$ and from the closed affine-simplex description [F6] when $d\ge2$. Choose a finite-radius ball containing the cell. By [F5] the ball is Lebesgue measurable with finite measure, while [F8] makes the cell measurable; [F9] and [F10] then give $\lambda_d(K)\le\lambda_d(B)<\infty$.

The full-support condition in step 1.2 and finite-measure condition in step 1.3 let us invoke the cellwise projection lemma [F11] on every cell. Since $u(t,\cdot)$ is continuous and each cell has finite measure, it belongs to $L^2(K)$; hence $\Pi_hu$ is well defined.

Set $	heta=u_h-\Pi_hu$, so $u_h-u=	heta+\eta$. Subtract the exact weak equation in step 1.1 from [F1] and test with $v_h=	heta$. To justify differentiating projection orthogonality [F2], choose a monomial basis $\{\phi_i\}$ of $\mathbb P_p(K)$ and its fixed Gram matrix. By the construction in [F11], the projection coefficients solve that fixed finite linear system with moments $\int_Ku(t)\phi_i\,dx$. Since $u_t$ is continuous on the compact space-time cell, [F12] and uniform continuity show that the difference quotients of $u$ converge uniformly in $x$ to $u_t$; the bounded test polynomials and finite measure from step 1.3 therefore allow passage through each moment integral. The coefficients, and hence $\Pi_Ku$, are differentiable in time, so differentiating [F2] gives $(\eta_t,	heta)_K=0$. If $p=0$, then $
abla	heta=0$; if $p\ge1$, then $
abla	heta\in\mathbb P_{p-1}(K)^d$. Since $ eta$ is constant, in either case $ eta\cdot
abla	heta\in\mathbb P_p(K)$ and $(\eta, eta\cdot
abla	heta)_K=0$. This leaves only the transport error and the upwind face-flux differences.

Integrate the remaining $-(\beta\theta,\nabla\theta)_K$ by parts using [F3] for $d\ge2$ and [F12] on intervals for $d=1$, then pair cells using [F4] for $d\ge2$ or the endpoint convention in [F7] for $d=1$. By the face flux differences from step 3.1, inflow contributes no projection residual because both fluxes use $g$; interior and outflow residuals move to the right with signs $+\int_F(\beta\cdot n_F)\eta^{\mathrm{up}}[\theta]$ and $-\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)\eta\theta$, respectively. Hence
$$\frac12\frac d{dt}\|\theta\|_2^2+\frac12\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{int}}}\int_F|\beta\cdot n_F|[\theta]^2+\frac12\int_{\Gamma_-}|\beta\cdot n|\theta^2+\frac12\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)\theta^2=\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{int}}}\int_F(\beta\cdot n_F)\eta^{\mathrm{up}}[\theta]-\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)\eta\theta.$$

For each interior face use $|b||\eta^{\mathrm{up}}||[\theta]|\le\frac{|b|}{4}[\theta]^2+|b||\eta^{\mathrm{up}}|^2$, and on outflow use $b|\eta||\theta|\le\frac b4\theta^2+b|\eta|^2$. Write $v=\nabla\eta$ and $\psi_\ell=v^TF_\ell-q_\ell$. For every direction, supply a symmetric consistent two-point flux $F_\ell^{ec}$ satisfying [[def-pe03-tadmor-entropy-conservative-flux]], namely
$$\bigl(v(U_R)-v(U_L)\bigr)^TF_\ell^{ec}(U_L,U_R)=\psi_\ell(U_R)-\psi_\ell(U_L).$$

On each cell use diagonal-norm SBP data from [[def-pe04-diagonal-norm-sbp-element-data]]. Put $Q_{K,\ell}=H_KD_{K,\ell}$; let $U_i^K\in\mathcal A$ be the nodal states; and let the face restrictions select paired face nodes with matching positive weights on the two incident cells. For an oriented interior face node with normal $n$ from the minus trace to the plus trace, set $F_n(U)=\sum_\ell n_\ell F_\ell(U)$ and $\psi_n(U)=\sum_\ell n_\ell\psi_\ell(U)$. Given any fixed coefficient $\alpha_{F,q}\ge0$, define the normal interface flux
$$\widehat F_{n,F,q}^*(U^-,U^+)=\sum_{\ell=1}^d n_\ell F_\ell^{ec}(U^-,U^+)-\frac{\alpha_{F,q}}2\bigl(v(U^+)-v(U^-)\bigr).$$
The coefficient is the same when the face orientation is reversed. Thus the flux is conservative and consistent, and its entropy contraction is
$$[v]^T\widehat F_{n,F,q}^*=[\psi_n]-\frac{\alpha_{F,q}}2\lVert[v]\rVert^2\le[\psi_n],$$
by the directional Tadmor identities in [[def-pe03-tadmor-entropy-conservative-flux]]. On physical boundary faces supply a consistent normal flux and require the boundary entropy contribution below to be nonnegative.

Write $\omega_{F,q}$ for the $q$th diagonal entry of $M_F$. Define the boundary entropy contribution
$$\mathcal B_h(t)=\sum_{F\subset\partial\Omega}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}\bigl(v(U_{F,q})^T\widehat F_{n_F}^*-\psi_{n_F}(U_{F,q})\bigr).$$
The selected boundary flux is entropy admissible when $\mathcal B_h(t)\ge0$. The **flux-differencing SBP semidiscretization** on each element is
$$H_K\dot U^K+2\sum_{\ell=1}^d\bigl(Q_{K,\ell}\circ F_\ell^{ec}(U^K,U^K)\bigr)\mathbf1+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}R_{K,F}^TM_{K,F}\bigl(\widehat F_{n_{K,F}}^*-F_{n_{K,F}}(U_{K,F})\bigr)=0,$$
where $\circ$ is entrywise matrix multiplication and $F_\ell^{ec}(U^K,U^K)$ is the matrix with $(i,j)$ entry $F_\ell^{ec}(U_i^K,U_j^K)$. These are conditional method data: compatible SBP data and directional entropy-conservative fluxes are hypotheses, not asserted to exist for every mesh or entropy pair. Symmetry of $F_\ell^{ec}$ from [F4] gives $2\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}v_i^TF_{ij}^{ec}=\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}(v_i-v_j)^TF_{ij}^{ec}+\sum_{i,j}(Q_{ij}+Q_{ji})v_j^TF_{ij}^{ec}$. By [F4] the first sum is $\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}(\psi_i-\psi_j)=-\sum_j\psi_j(Q^T\mathbf1)_j=-\sum_F\sum_q\omega_{F,q}\psi_{n_F}(U_{F,q})$, since $Q\mathbf1=0$ and $Q^T\mathbf1=(Q+Q^T)\mathbf1$ by [F2]. The second sum is $\sum_F\sum_q\omega_{F,q}v(U_{F,q})^TF_{n_F}(U_{F,q})$ by [F2], diagonal face selection, and consistency from [F4]. Summing directions and the potential identity in [F3] proves the volume entropy boundary identity.

The chain rule gives $\frac{d}{dt}\sum_iH_{ii}\eta(U_i)=\sum_iH_{ii}v(U_i)^T\dot U_i$. Since the semidiscrete equation is $H\dot U+V+SAT=0$, the entropy rate is the negative of the volume and SAT contractions. Combining the volume contraction from step 1.1 with $-v^TR^TM(\widehat F_n^*-F_n)$ cancels the physical flux and leaves, on each cell face, $\sum_q\omega_{F,q}(\psi_{n_F}(U_{F,q})-v(U_{F,q})^T\widehat F_{n_F,q}^*)$.

Moving these terms to the left gives the asserted identity, and [A1] gives nonincrease.

For each component, the constant-vector contraction of the volume term is $2\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}F^{ec}(U_i,U_j)=\sum_{i,j}(Q_{ij}+Q_{ji})F^{ec}(U_i,U_j)$. Its interior contributions cancel by normal reversal from the interface formula [F1]; identified periodic boundary partners cancel in the same way. Therefore the periodic quadrature-weighted total state is constant.

If the evaluator reports failure, return evaluation-failure with that stage index. Execute:

1. Query $f(t,y)$. On success set $Y_1=y+h f(t,y)$.
2. Query $f(t+h,Y_1)$. On success set $Y_2=\frac34y+\frac14\bigl(Y_1+h f(t+h,Y_1)\bigr)$.
3. Query $f(t+h/2,Y_2)$. On success set $y^+=\frac13y+\frac23\bigl(Y_2+h f(t+h/2,Y_2)\bigr)$.

Let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite periodic matching affine simplicial mesh in $d\ge2$, let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and apply [[alg-pe04-first-order-upwind-forward-euler]] with $\lambda_K\le1$ for every cell. For every convex function $\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the weighted discrete entropy does not increase:

A subset $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is **convex** when, for all $x,y\in U$ and $t\in[0,1]$ ([[def-interval]]), the point $(1-t)x+ty$ lies in $U$. Thus the full line segment from $x$ to $y$ remains in $U$.

Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be convex ([[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]). The function $f:C\to\mathbb R$ is convex when $f((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)$ for all $x,y\in C$ and $t\in[0,1]$. The parameter interval is the closed interval of [[def-interval]].

It is strictly convex when the inequality is strict for distinct $x,y$ and $0<t<1$. No strict inequality is required at $t=0$ or $t=1$, where the two sides coincide. The empty set and a singleton support convex functions, and strict convexity on either is vacuous.

Let $d\ge2$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh whose boundary faces are paired by translations to form a periodic mesh, let $V_K=\int_K1\,dx$ be cell volume, and let $A_F=\int_F1\,dS$ be face area. Let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and let $U_K\in\mathbb R$ be one cell mean per cell. For each face $F\subset\partial K$, let $n_{K,F}$ be the outward unit normal, $b_{K,F}=\beta\cdot n_{K,F}$, and $K_F$ the neighboring cell across that periodic face. With $b^+=\max(b,0)$ and $b^- =\min(b,0)$, the upwind flux out of $K$ is
$$\widehat f_{K,F}=b_{K,F}^+U_K+b_{K,F}^-U_{K_F}.$$
For a step $\Delta t>0$, first compute
$$\lambda_K=\frac{\Delta t}{V_K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}A_Fb_{K,F}^+.$$
The **degree-zero upwind forward-Euler update** is admissible when $\lambda_K\le1$ for every cell; its output is
$$U_K^+=U_K-\frac{\Delta t}{V_K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}A_F\widehat f_{K,F}.$$
This is the degree-zero specialization of [[def-pe04-upwind-dg-transport-discretization]].

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

On an affine element in dimension $d\ge1$, diagonal-norm SBP data consist of a nodal state vector with $N_K$ entries, a positive diagonal matrix $H_K\in\mathbb R^{N_K\times N_K}$, and derivative matrices $D_{K,\ell}$, $1\le\ell\le d$. Put $Q_{K,\ell}=H_KD_{K,\ell}$. For each face $F$ let $R_{K,F}$ select its face nodes from the volume nodes, let $M_{K,F}$ be a positive diagonal face quadrature matrix, and let $n_{K,F}$ be its constant outward unit normal. The data are **SBP compatible** when
$$D_{K,\ell}\mathbf1=0,\qquad R_{K,F}\mathbf1=\mathbf1_F,\qquad Q_{K,\ell}+Q_{K,\ell}^{T}=\sum_{F\subset\partial K} n_{K,F,\ell}R_{K,F}^{T}M_{K,F}R_{K,F}$$
for each coordinate $\ell$. The rows of $R_{K,F}$ select the nodes used by the face quadrature; on an interior face, the two cells have the same face nodes and weights under the face identification and opposite normals. In dimension one, $R_L$ and $R_R$ select the left and right endpoint nodes with normals $-1$ and $+1$.

This is conditional algebraic data: the definition does not assert that every mesh has such a rule. The identities include exact affine metric factors and no curved-element metric approximation.

derivations.claim: Direct multiplication gives $D\mathbf1=0$ and $HD+D^TH=\operatorname{diag}(-1,0,1)=B$, so the derivative and norm satisfy the stated SBP identity. The three-point Gauss–Lobatto rule is exact through degree three, while both the quadratic entropy integrand $u_h^2$ and cubic entropy flux $u_h^3$ exceed that degree for a quadratic polynomial; the pointwise collocation therefore underintegrates these nonlinear products.

At the chosen state, $f(U)=(9/2,1/2,2)^T$ and $\widehat f_{\partial}=13/4$. Hence $Df(U)=(-27/4,-5/4,17/4)^T$ and $H^{-1}B(\widehat f_{\partial}-f(U_{\partial}))=(15/4,0,15/4)^T$. The semidiscrete residual is therefore $(-3,-5/4,8)^T$, so $\dot U=(3,5/4,-8)^T$.

The discrete entropy rate is $\dot E=U^TH\dot U=(-3)(1/3)(3)+(-1)(4/3)(5/4)+(-2)(1/3)(-8)=2/3>0$. This exact periodic state contradicts the asserted universal nonincrease, despite the SBP identity; it does not contradict the entropy-stable flux-differencing theorem, which uses a different volume flux.

Fix constant transport velocity $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ and SBP data from [[def-pe04-diagonal-norm-sbp-element-data]]. For each cell $K$, let $U_K(t)$ be the vector of nodal values, $Q_{K,\ell}=H_KD_{K,\ell}$, and $U_{K,F}=R_{K,F}U_K$. Set $b_{K,F}=\beta\cdot n_{K,F}$. At each interior face, use the trace from the cell with positive outward speed when $b_{K,F}>0$, and the neighboring trace when $b_{K,F}<0$; at boundary faces use the inflow data on $b_{K,F}<0$ and the interior trace on $b_{K,F}\ge0$. Denote this upwind scalar trace by $\widehat U_{K,F}$.

The **upwind SBP-SAT semidiscretization** is
$$H_K\dot U_K+\sum_{\ell=1}^d\beta_\ell Q_{K,\ell}U_K+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}R_{K,F}^{T}M_{K,F}\,b_{K,F}(\widehat U_{K,F}-U_{K,F})=0.$$
The sign of the SAT correction is fixed by this equation. The definition is spatial only and makes no fully discrete claim.

Let $d\ge1$. If $d=1$, let the cells be a finite oriented interval mesh from [[def-pe04-one-dimensional-interval-mesh-and-broken-polynomials]]; if $d\ge2$, let them form a finite matching affine simplicial mesh. On every cell assume diagonal-norm SBP data of [[def-pe04-diagonal-norm-sbp-element-data]], with paired interior face nodes, equal paired weights, and opposite outward normals. Let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and let the differentiable nodal state $U_K(t)$ solve the upwind SBP-SAT method of [[def-pe04-upwind-sbp-sat-transport-discretization]] with prescribed inflow values $g_{F,q}$ where $b_{K,F}:=\beta\cdot n_{K,F}<0$. Write $\omega_{F,q}$ for the diagonal entries of the face norm. On an interior face oriented from $K^-$ to $K^+$, set $b_F=\beta\cdot n_F$ and $[U]_{F,q}=U^+_{F,q}-U^-_{F,q}$. Let $\Gamma_+$ and $\Gamma_-$ denote the boundary faces with positive and negative outward speed, respectively. For $d=1$, each face has one endpoint node and its face sum is a one-point sum. The discrete energy $E_h=\frac12\sum_K U_K^TH_KU_K$ satisfies
$$\frac{dE_h}{dt}+\frac12\sum_{F\text{ interior}}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_F|[U]_{F,q}^2+\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_+}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}b_{K,F}U_{F,q}^2+\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_-}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_{K,F}|(U_{F,q}-g_{F,q})^2=\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_-}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_{K,F}|g_{F,q}^2.$$
Consequently, zero inflow data give a nonincreasing SBP norm.
